body:
The same gap exists on the focus side. With:

```html
<input id="a">
<input id="b" onfocus="c.focus()">
<input id="c">
<script> a.focus(); b.focus(); </script>
```

…WebKit, Chrome, and Firefox all end with `c` focused and fire blur a, focusout a, focus b, blur b, focusout b, focus c, focusin c — and no focusin at `b`. As written, nothing in the focus update steps stops after the nested focusing steps run from `b`’s focus handler, so the outer run continues through its remaining new-chain entries, and once #10235 lands it would also fire a focusin at `b` that no browser fires. Blink’s `Document::SetFocusedElement` and WebKit’s `Document::setFocusedElement` return on “handler shifted focus” after each event; Gecko’s `FocusInOutEvent::Run` drops a focusin whose target is no longer the focused element.

Ladybird hit this on github.com; see https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/12477: A focus trap moves focus from inside the focus event, the extra focusin fed a second focus manager, and the two recursed until the call stack died. So the guard matters for the focusin step in #10235 as well as for the blur case above.
